title: NCP local simulation reference
subtitle: An illustrated guide to causality, evidence, and bounded execution
status: First bounded development profile. Final product v1 requirements and qualification remain open.

pages.title: One reference experiment. Four owners.
pages.intro: This bounded development example connects four native owners. Final v1 still requires optional project combinations, profiles for many entities and sensor modalities, and Prisoma experiment ownership.

sections.heading: Who does the work?
sections.text: Engram coordinates the experiment and privately owns NEST. CREBAIN owns the body and fusion kernels. Prisoma captures evidence. Galadriel runs its detector.

sections.heading: What does NCP own?
sections.text: NCP supplies the shared profile, bounded messages, exact outcome retention, and independent decoder contract. It is not another application orchestrator.

sections.heading: Read the boundary
sections.text: This reference profile admits local direct simulation with record-only monitoring. Remote control, physical actuation, Haldir gating, and real-time guarantees remain excluded from this profile.

pages.title: A command needs the correct predecessor.
pages.intro: A fast message can still carry the wrong causal step. First establish what each command depends on, then measure transmission cost.

equations.explanation: The encoder E maps observation x into neural input. N advances persistent neural state z. Decoder D produces the next proposed action u. Observation x has per-component position and velocity units. Neural state z uses the installed model units. Action u has acceleration components.
Body transition F consumes that proposal and returns the next observation. The subscripts identify logical boundaries, not wall-clock completion times.

sections.heading: A small delay can change stability
sections.text: Consider the dimensionless teaching model x[k+1] = x[k] + u[k+1], with u[k+1] = -1.5 x[k]. Its multiplier is -0.5, so errors shrink.

sections.heading: Use the previous sample by mistake
sections.text: A one-step stale command gives x[k+1] = x[k] - 1.5 x[k-1]. The characteristic roots have magnitude sqrt(1.5), approximately 1.225. Errors grow.

sections.heading: Scope of this example
sections.text: This calculation proves behavior of the stated recurrence. It is not a stability proof for the NEST controller or the CREBAIN body.

pages.title: Logical time and recorded spikes.
pages.intro: A logical clock counts declared simulator advances. A wall clock measures elapsed execution. Pausing a deterministic experiment does not advance its logical clock.

equations.explanation: k is the completed step count. h is the step duration in integer microseconds. r is the NEST integration resolution in the same unit.
delta is the admitted recording delay. W is the completed readout interval. The left endpoint is excluded and the right endpoint is included.

sections.heading: Worked clock example
sections.text: For h = 20,000 microseconds and r = 100 microseconds, each step contains exactly 200 integration intervals. After 128 steps, t = 2.56 seconds.

sections.heading: Worked readout example
sections.text: With a 1,000-microsecond delay, the first windows are (0, 19] milliseconds and (19, 39] milliseconds. A spike at 19 milliseconds belongs only to the first.

sections.heading: Persistent state needs a real test
sections.text: Keep the actual NEST network between steps. Test the selected stimulus update mechanism on the exact installed build. Do not assume every runtime mutation is legal.

sections.heading: Do not mix clock domains
sections.text: Subtract timestamps only when their clock origin and meaning agree. A coordinator round trip is not automatically body-source-to-application latency.

pages.title: NIS measures scaled residual magnitude.
pages.intro: Normalized innovation squared (NIS) compares a prediction error with its declared uncertainty. It does not turn a finite number into calibrated evidence.

equations.explanation: e is the three-dimensional innovation in meters. S is its covariance in square meters. q and the innovation dimension d are dimensionless.
This diagonal covariance gives three separate squared terms. It is a teaching input, not a retained CREBAIN measurement.
Each squared residual is scaled by its variance. Changing units consistently changes e and S together, leaving q unchanged.

sections.heading: Assumptions before probability
sections.text: The chi-square reference requires a justified Gaussian innovation model and positive definite covariance. Finite matrix entries alone establish neither condition.

sections.heading: Three dimensions are one modality
sections.text: CREBAIN's selected adapter supplies one Visual NIS value with d = 3. This is one sensor modality, not three independent modalities.

pages.title: A detector must be allowed to abstain.
pages.intro: The local Galadriel adapter invokes the actual SubsetMagnitudeV0_9 engine. It preserves its research classification and the unchanged evidence minimum.

equations.plain: Q = sum of q[i], for i = 1 through n; reference Q ~ chi-square(n*d)
equations.explanation: n counts accepted observations in one channel window. The reference also needs the stated temporal independence assumptions and fixed innovation dimension d. Index i runs from one through n. The chi-square reference has n times d degrees of freedom.

equations.plain: 64 samples * 3 NIS units per sample = 192; reference dimension = 64*3 = 192
equations.explanation: This synthetic arithmetic matches the reference mean. It does not establish model validity, temporal independence, or cross-modal consistency.

sections.heading: The actual evidence floor
sections.text: The unchanged named detector uses a 64-sample window, at least 32 samples, and at least two modalities. One Visual channel remains InsufficientEvidence.

sections.heading: Birth is not a zero residual
sections.text: Track birth has no prior innovation. The adapter returns not_ready without creating a detector observation. A later actual update starts an empty window.

sections.heading: Loss retires the window
sections.text: Missing evidence after activation retires that entity's window for the complete endpoint generation. Later observations cannot silently restore readiness.

sections.heading: Evidence is not permission
sections.text: Even a favorable synthetic detector control grants no command, lease, reset, or policy authority. calibrated_posterior stays false.

pages.title: Know the outcome before advancing.
pages.intro: A lost response does not reveal whether execution happened. Exact retained outcomes let a caller recover known work without executing it twice.

sections.heading: Before execution
sections.text: The owner checks the binding, plan, operation, sequence, data, and available response slot. A rejection at this stage performs no backend mutation.

sections.heading: After known completion
sections.text: The owner retains the complete response. An identical retry returns those bytes. A changed retry conflicts. A successor waits for the exact result acknowledgement.

sections.heading: After uncertainty
sections.text: An execution exception, unrepresentable result, or unresolved process failure retires mutable state. Cancellation does not mean rollback. Dependent owners cannot continue an uncertain experiment.

sections.heading: After acknowledgement
sections.text: The payload may be released. The retained high-water state still prevents re-execution. A later lookup returns unavailable rather than a reconstructed result.

sections.heading: Coordinator audit journal
sections.text: Engram records dispatch intent before sending. It records the response before coordinator progress. Unresolved loss leaves an unknown-outcome record. This owner-local journal supports audit. It grants no peer integration route or authority to resume uncertain state.

equations.plain: result digest = hash(domain || canonical(response without result_digest))
equations.explanation: R is the complete response. D_R is its result_digest field. Excluding only that field avoids a circular definition while covering the whole result body. H is SHA-256. The double bar concatenates the domain separator and typed canonical bytes.

pages.closing: The typed canonical encoding preserves exact integers and binary64 values. A one-bit probability change is a digest failure, not harmless formatting.

pages.title: A complete subset can hide an incomplete run.
pages.intro: Individually valid rows are insufficient. A capture must prove its declared roster, every contiguous step pair, and a matching terminal record.

equations.plain: P is the largest step such that every step 1 through P is known closed
equations.explanation: A step is closed only after its required neural, body, and capture outcomes are known and joined. A later row cannot fill an earlier gap. The empty prefix has length zero. Index p ranges from zero through planned count N.

equations.plain: complete = matching terminal AND closed prefix equals planned count AND valid joins AND no unknown suffix
equations.explanation: T means the terminal record matches the plan. N is the planned step count. J means every causal join validates. U means an unresolved mutation remains. C is the Boolean capture-completeness result.

sections.heading: Worked missing-step example
sections.text: A four-step plan retains valid rows 1, 2, and 4. Its maximal closed prefix is 2. Three valid rows do not prove four completed steps.

sections.heading: Worked terminal example
sections.text: All four rows exist, but the terminal record is absent or conflicts. Completeness remains unresolved or invalid. Do not infer a successful finish.

sections.heading: Capture before progress
sections.text: Reserve required evidence capacity before neural or body mutation. If the reservation fails, pause or reject at that declared boundary.

pages.title: Bounds and measurements need honest names.
pages.intro: A structural buffer bound is not a resident-memory measurement. An observed percentile is not a guarantee about future deadlines.

equations.plain: retained wire payload <= 4 endpoints * 65,536 bytes = 256 KiB
equations.explanation: E is the endpoint count and F is the maximum result frame. This bound excludes parsed objects, pipe buffers, simulator state, and captured history.

equations.plain: source-to-effect latency = body application time minus body source time
equations.explanation: Both timestamps need the same body-owned clock and the specified event boundaries. A coordinator request timer measures a different interval. T is elapsed time in seconds. Both timestamps use the same unit.

sections.heading: Measure a paired comparison
sections.text: Run matched direct and NCP trials with the same logical inputs, seed, build, and instrumentation. Compare paired differences rather than subtracting unrelated percentiles.

sections.heading: Publish the observation
sections.text: Report sample count, p50, p99, p99.9, maximum, failures, host, worker placement, and instrumentation. State untested loads and all excluded timing guarantees.

sections.heading: Keep the release gate visible
sections.text: The 70-case mapping tracks local requirements and enforced exclusions. Final native, containment, installed-artifact, and reproduction receipts remain open in this guide.

sections.heading: What this guide proves
sections.text: The worked calculations explain their stated models. Diagrams and numerical examples are not substitute evidence for an installed NCP release.

pages.closing: Read the adjacent README.md, decision.md, and acceptance-70.md for this reference profile, open product requirements, and every required acceptance control.
